statusText: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Tail is elevated during the immediate post-FOMC late-repricing window.
recommendation: Current policy mapping is BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES; the elevated state reflects the late post-FOMC equity/rates reversal, with de-escalation conditional on two-way price discovery and meaningful retracements.
headline: Late post-FOMC reversal lifts Tail into the elevated band
body: The Fed raised its target range 25 basis points to 3.75%-4.00% and signaled further tightening risk. Reuters reported late stock and bond selling; AP reported the Nasdaq down 0.5% and S&P 500 down 0.8% after earlier gains reversed, while short Treasury yields rose. Oil fell roughly 3%, limiting full cross-asset alignment. Direct live NQ retracement microstructure was not independently available, but the observed late equity reversal, firmer rates/dollar and credible FOMC second-leg mechanism justify a minimal elevated Tail reading rather than a higher band.

lookbackSummary: All 24 prior UTC clock-hour slots are available. Tail stayed between 17% and 24%; Stress remained 99%-100%. The regime was mostly mixed, with WATCH/event-whipsaw readings around the U.S. data and FOMC sequence and Tail at 24% in both the 18:00 and 19:00 UTC hours.
outlookSummary: Immediate risk is concentrated in the late post-FOMC/post-close repricing window, where the observed equity reversal and firmer rates create a credible delayed second leg. Tail is expected to fall back toward WATCH and then low if retracements become functional. Thursday's 12:30 UTC labor, housing and Philadelphia Fed cluster raises Stress before it raises Tail.

forecast.analysis: Fed-day equities reversed from earlier gains: Reuters reported late selling after the 25 bp hike, while AP had Nasdaq down 0.5% and S&P 500 down 0.8%. Treasury yields rose, but oil fell sharply. Direct live NQ retracement microstructure is unavailable; the aligned post-FOMC second leg lifts Tail into elevated.

forecastDetail.comment: Late post-FOMC equity weakness, firmer yields and a stronger dollar create an elevated delayed-second-leg risk, while falling oil and unavailable live NQ microstructure cap the score.
The immediate post-close window remains elevated only if the late selloff extends with shallow retracements and rates confirmation; two-way trade would de-escalate the path.
The base case moves back to WATCH as the FOMC impulse ages; renewed rates-and-dollar alignment with fresh equity extension would keep second-leg risk active.
Residual policy repricing can remain volatile in thinner liquidity, but a retracement of the late selloff would weaken the delayed-second-leg case.
By midnight UTC, normalization is the base case: two-way price discovery returns Tail below WATCH even though policy and inflation keep Stress extreme.
Overnight Tail continues to ease unless another directional futures leg appears with rates confirmation or a fresh geopolitical shock.
